design_status: phase2-conform: Numbered Ledger approved (E1-E7); back-design.md delivered; oracle EXACT; prototype scope p1c10+p1c11

p1c10.mood_arc: The storm breaks: longest chapter must feel monumental — rank made visible, then the 'EVIL thoughts' finale releases the pressure.
p1c10.opener: CONFORMED in back-design.md §3 p1c10 (ledger grammar); was: PROVISIONAL: stepped ascent composition behind the title — pathos of distance rendered as vertical hierarchy; long-chapter relief via aphorism-number styling.
p1c10.rationale: The book's longest chapter (§257–296) is a doctrine of rank: 'EVERY elevation of the type man has hitherto been the work of an aristocratic society' (§257), 'the PATHOS OF DISTANCE' (§257), 'INSTINCT FOR RANK' (§263), solitude (§289: recluse/echo of the wilderness), masks (§269–270), and the closing cry to 'my old, beloved— EVIL thoughts!' (§296). Verbatim: 'EVERY elevation of the type "man," has hitherto been the work of an aristocratic society' (§257); 'you sudden sparks and marvels of my solitude, you, my old, beloved-- EVIL thoughts!' (§296). Treatment must carry scale, height, and hardness — not the storm's rain but its summit.
p1c10.reading: CONFORMED in back-design.md §3 p1c10 (ledger grammar); was: PROVISIONAL: ascending section markers keyed to rank motif; relief rhythm for ~94 paragraphs.
key_passages: §278: 'Wanderer, who art thou? I see thee follow thy path without scorn, without love, with unfathomable eyes, wet and sad as a plummet which has returned to the light insatiated out of every depth' — the plummet-from-depth image.
§284: 'To live in a vast and proud tranquility; always beyond… to SEAT oneself on them as upon horses' + 'solitude is a virtue with us, as a sublime bent and bias to purity.'
§295: 'the genius of the heart… which smoothes rough souls and makes them taste a new longing--to lie placid as a mirror, that the deep heavens may be reflected in them.'
p1c10.gloss: Rank, distance, and the noble soul.

p1c11.mood_arc: Resolution: light, altitude, intimacy. The one chapter that is song, not argument — midday sun after the storm.
p1c11.opener:
CONFORMED in back-design.md §3 p1c11 (ledger grammar); was: PROVISIONAL: luminous alpine composition — glacier/eagle/height; verse-first layout with generous measure and stanza breathing (plain

per line, styled as verse).
p1c11.rationale: A 36-line alpine poem, not prose: 'MIDDAY of Life! Oh, season of delight!', 'Is not the glacier's grey today for you / Rose-garlanded?', 'To spy for you from farthest eagle's view', the bow-and-arrow huntsman ('An evil huntsman was I? See how taut / My bow was bent!'), and the finale 'friend Zarathustra, came!' Verbatim: 'MIDDAY of Life! Oh, season of delight!'; 'The Guest of Guests, friend Zarathustra, came!' Treatment MUST be verse-luminous — stanza rhythm, altitude, noon light — never a prose wall.
p1c11.reading: CONFORMED in back-design.md §3 p1c11 (ledger grammar); was: PROVISIONAL: verse measure, restrained italic/indent cadence for stanza groups, no drop cap.
key_passages: 'My table was spread out for you on high-- / Who dwelleth so Star-near, so near the grisly pit below?' — height-above-abyss, the cohort's final vertical image.
'Midday of life! My second youth's delight!' + 'At midday 'twas, when one became as two' — noon as transformation.
Close: 'The world now laughs, the grisly veil was torn, / And Light and Dark were one that wedding-morn.'
p1c11.gloss: NONE — the poem's first line is the gloss.

p1c6.mood_arc: The storm gathers low: herds, obedience, discipline — earth-bound pressure that the later chapters release upward.
p1c6.opener: CONFORMED in back-design.md §3 p1c6 (ledger grammar); was: PROVISIONAL: specimen-field composition behind the title — many small disciplined forms (the 'MANY kinds of morality') under one gathering pressure; aphorism numerals styled as catalogue entries.
p1c6.rationale: The chapter is a naturalist's cabinet of moralities: 'the problem of morality itself has been OMITTED' from every 'Science of Morals' (§186); morals as 'tyranny against nature' bred by 'long OBEDIENCE' (§188); the herd instinct — 'there have also been human herds (family alliances, communities, tribes, peoples, states, churches)' (§199); master/slave valuations; and the closing 'storms which sweep across the heaven of OUR life' (§203). Verbatim: 'problems which only disclose themselves by a comparison of MANY kinds of morality' (§186); 'there have also been human herds' (§199). Treatment should feel taxonomic and loamy — many specimens, disciplined ranks, gathering weight.
p1c6.reading: CONFORMED in back-design.md §3 p1c6 (ledger grammar); was: PROVISIONAL: catalogue-like aphorism numbers (§186–203), disciplined measure, specimen-plate dividers.
key_passages: §196: 'It is to be INFERRED that there are countless dark bodies near the sun--such as we shall never see… the psychologist of morals reads the whole star-writing merely as an allegorical and symbolic language' — NOTE: p1c6 has its own astronomical image; coordinate with p1c8's two-suns motif so they differ (dark bodies/occlusion vs twin-sun motley light).
§197: 'The beast of prey and the man of prey (for instance, Caesar Borgia)… the healthiest of all tropical monsters and growths' + 'Morals as Timidity' — tropical/temperate contrast.
§203 close: 'these are the heavy distant thoughts and storms which sweep across the heaven of OUR life.'

p1c7.mood_arc: The satirist's laboratory: cold instruments under glass — the scholar diminished against the philosopher's elevation.
p1c7.opener: CONFORMED in back-design.md §3 p1c7 (ledger grammar); was: PROVISIONAL: instrument-cabinet composition — lenses/slides/specimen jars rendered small and cold; title set against the 'elevation' the scholar cannot reach.
p1c7.rationale: A satire of the learned man as the philosopher's decadent shadow: the 'OBJECTIVE spirit' sick 'of all subjectivity' (§207); the scholar as mere 'instrument' (8x) and specialist who has 'specialize[d]' himself away from 'superspection, circumspection, DESPECTION' (§205); 'philosophical workers, and in general scientific men' confounded with philosophers (§211); Napoleon's 'VOILA UN HOMME!' on Goethe (§209); closing on breeding and 'gradation of rank' (§213). Verbatim: 'one might doubt whether this fruit could still come to maturity' (§205); 'VOILA UN HOMME!' (§209). Treatment should feel like a cold instrument cabinet — precise, diminishing, faintly comic.
p1c7.reading: CONFORMED in back-design.md §3 p1c7 (ledger grammar); was: PROVISIONAL: clinical aphorism numbers, footnote-like asides feel, one warm accent reserved for the Goethe moment.
key_passages: §205: 'The dangers that beset the evolution of the philosopher are, in fact, so manifold nowadays, that one might doubt whether this fruit could still come to maturity.'
§213 close: 'they have to be BRED for it… Many generations must have prepared the way for the coming of the philosopher' — breeding motif links forward to p1c10 rank.
p1c7.gloss: The scholar is an instrument — not a philosopher.

p1c8.mood_arc: The sky opens: two suns, motley light — the cohort's first genuinely beautiful image, before the nations chapter complicates it.
p1c8.opener: CONFORMED in back-design.md §3 p1c8 (ledger grammar); was: PROVISIONAL: twin-sun firmament composition — 'we Europeans of the day after tomorrow' under two differently coloured suns; title lit motley.
p1c8.rationale: Opens 'OUR Virtues?' for 'we Europeans of the day after tomorrow' (§214) and gives the cohort its single most paintable image: 'As in the stellar firmament there are sometimes two suns which determine the path of one planet… suns of different colours shine around a single planet, now with red light, now with green… our actions are MOTLEY-COLOURED' (§215). Also the 'granite of spiritual fate' (§231), the tediousness of moralists (§228: 'virtue has been MORE injured by the TEDIOUSNESS of its advocates'), and the tiger-clawed 'dangerous and beautiful cat, woman' finale (§239). Verbatim: 'there are sometimes two suns which determine the path of one planet' (§215); 'at the bottom of our souls… a granite of spiritual fate' (§231). Treatment: a motley firmament — dual-coloured light on one planet.
p1c8.reading: CONFORMED in back-design.md §3 p1c8 (ledger grammar); was: PROVISIONAL: sun-pair section markers; granite-dark pull-moments for §231; restrained handling of the §232–239 polemic (no caricature).
key_passages: §215: 'As in the stellar firmament there are sometimes two suns which determine the path of one planet, and in certain cases suns of different colours shine around a single planet, now with red light, now with green' — the cohort's signature image; must differ from p1c6 §196 dark-bodies image.
§231: 'at the bottom of our souls, quite down below, there is certainly something unteachable, a granite of spiritual fate.'
§226: 'WE IMMORALISTS.--This world… this almost invisible, inaudible world of delicate command.'
p1c8.gloss: Two suns, one planet: our motley-coloured actions.

p1c9.mood_arc: The orchestra tunes then overreaches: Wagner's pride, national portraits in sequence, ending in Rome-satire — the cohort's most theatrical movement.
p1c9.opener: CONFORMED in back-design.md §3 p1c9 (ledger grammar); was: PROVISIONAL: overture composition — score-like staves or a conductor's surge behind the title; national 'movements' signalled as the chapter proceeds.
p1c9.rationale: Opens on Wagner's Mastersinger overture — 'a piece of magnificent, gorgeous, heavy, latter-day art' (§240) — then marches through Germans ('THEY HAVE AS YET NO TODAY', §240; 94x 'German'), 'good Europeans' (§241), Jews (§250), English (§252), France 'the high school of taste' (§254), and tempo/march motifs (§255), closing with the satirical Rome verse ('ROME'S FAITH BY INTUITION!'). Verbatim: 'I HEARD, once again for the first time, Richard Wagner's overture to the Mastersinger' (§240); 'they belong to the day before yesterday and the day after tomorrow' (§240). Treatment: an overture — musical surge, national movements, theatrical close.
p1c9.reading: CONFORMED in back-design.md §3 p1c9 (ledger grammar); was: PROVISIONAL: movement-like section markers per nation; score-inflected dividers; verse styling for the closing Rome stanza.
key_passages: §243: 'I hear with pleasure that our sun is moving rapidly towards the constellation Hercules: and I hope that the men on this earth will do like the sun. And we foremost, we good Europeans!' — third solar image in the cohort; keep distinct (a sun in motion/voyage).
§245: 'The good old time is past, it sang itself out in Mozart-- how happy are WE that his ROCOCO still speaks to us' — rococo/Mozart counter-motif to Wagner's heaviness.
Close: Rome satire-verse ending 'For what ye hear is ROME-- ROME'S FAITH BY INTUITION!' — theatrical verse finale.
p1c9.gloss: An overture on Germans, neighbours, and good Europeans.

mood_arc: LOWLAND → LABORATORY → FIRMAMENT → OVERTURE → SUMMIT → NOON: the cohort climbs from the herds and obedience of p1c6, through the scholar's cold cabinet (p1c7), up into the twin-sun sky of p1c8, through the national orchestra of p1c9, to the aristocratic summit of longest chapter p1c10, and resolves in the alpine midday poem of p1c11 — height and light increasing across the arc.
